title: The Town Musicians of Bremen.
lines: Once upon a time there was a donkey.
He had worked hard for the miller all his life.
Every day he carried heavy sacks of flour to the mill.
But now he had grown old.
His back hurt and he couldn't walk so fast anymore.
The miller said: You're too old.
I don't need you anymore.
The donkey was sad.
But then he had an idea.
I still have a fine voice, he thought.
Hee-haw, hee-haw!
I'm going to the town of Bremen.
I'll be a musician there!
And off he went.
On the way he saw a dog lying by the road.
The dog was panting.
What's wrong, friend?
asked the donkey.
Oh, said the dog.
I'm old.
I can't hunt anymore.
My master doesn't want me anymore.
Come with me to Bremen, said the donkey.
We'll be musicians.
I'll play the lute, and you'll play the drum.
The dog wagged his tail.
Woof!
Good idea!
They walked on together.
A little later they saw a cat.
She was sitting on a wall and looked very sad.
What's the matter, old cat?
they asked.
I'm old, miaowed the cat.
My teeth are blunt.
I can't catch mice anymore.
My mistress doesn't want me anymore.
Come with us to Bremen, said the donkey and the dog.
You sing so beautifully at night.
The cat jumped off the wall.
Miaow!
Then they came past a farm.
A rooster was sitting on the gate.
He was crowing as loud as he could.
Cock-a-doodle-doo!
Why are you crowing so loudly?
asked the friends.
Visitors are coming tomorrow, said the rooster.
And the farmer's wife wants to make soup out of me!
So I'm crowing as loud as I can one last time.
Come with us!
they said.
To Bremen!
With your voice we'll be famous.
The rooster flew off the gate.
Cock-a-doodle-doo!
And so the four of them walked on.
The donkey, the dog, the cat and the rooster.
But the town of Bremen was far away.
It got dark.
They came to a big forest.
There they saw a little light among the trees.
It was a house.
They crept up to it.
The donkey was the biggest.
He looked through the window.
What can you see?
asked the rooster.
I can see a table full of food, said the donkey.
Bread, cheese, sausage and cake.
And there are robbers sitting at the table.
Four robbers, counting their stolen gold.
Oh, how hungry the animals were.
They came up with a plan.
The donkey put his front legs on the windowsill.
The dog jumped onto the donkey's back.
The cat climbed onto the dog's back.
And the rooster flew onto the cat's head.
Then they all began to sing at the same time.
The donkey brayed: Hee-haw, hee-haw!
The dog barked: Woof, woof!
The cat miaowed: Miaow!
And the rooster crowed: Cock-a-doodle-doo!
And then they jumped in through the window.
Crash, tinkle, boom!
The robbers got the fright of their lives.
A monster!
they shouted.
A ghost!
And they ran into the forest as fast as they could.
The four friends sat down at the table.
They ate and ate, until their tummies were completely round.
Then they went to sleep.
The donkey in the stable, the dog behind the door, the cat by the warm fireplace, and the rooster on the roof.
In the middle of the night one robber came back.
He crept inside.
But the cat scratched him.
The dog bit his leg.
The donkey gave him a kick.
And the rooster crowed: Cock-a-doodle-doo!
The robber ran away and told the others: There's a witch living there, a man with a knife, a monster and a judge who shouts: bring that rascal here!
The robbers never came back.
And the four friends?
They never got to Bremen.
They liked the little house in the forest so much that they stayed there.
And every evening they made music together.
The end.
